01 / VOCAL MIXING — 100% FREE

TRANSMISSION PROTOCOL

How to Prepare & Send Your Stems

Following these steps ensures your session opens cleanly and sounds as high-quality as possible.

01

Completely Unedited Takes

Export all vocal files as they were recorded. Do not cut out breaths or slice syllables awkwardly. I need the full natural flow of your takes so timing and phase remain intact.

02

100% Dry — No Effects Added

Make sure all plugins are bypassed prior to export. No reverb, no delay, no EQ, and no baked-in autotune. Stems must be completely dry so they can be processed and shaped cleanly in the mix.

03

Export All Tracks from 0:00

Every single stem must start at the very beginning of the project timeline (0:00 / Bar 1). This ensures every vocal take, double, and adlib drops into place in sync with the beat.

04

Share Your Vision & Reference

Tell me what you want the song to feel like. Send 1–2 reference songs (SoundCloud, Spotify, or YouTube links) with the vocal presence, tone, or style you’re inspired by.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Collaboration FAQ

Do you make beats, melodies, or guitar loops?+

No. I do not produce melodic loops, sample packs, or create instrumentals from scratch. My focus is strictly on vocal mixing & engineering and vocal guest features over your existing beat.

What file formats should I send?+

Please send uncompressed WAV files (24-bit or 16-bit, 44.1kHz or 48kHz). Send your instrumental beat as a separate WAV or high-quality MP3. If you know the song’s BPM and musical key, include those as well.

What about mastering? Is mastering included?+

Vocal mixing is completely free. Final commercial mastering and streaming distribution (Spotify, Apple Music) are not included—those remain in your hands. However, I provide a balanced, clean stereo mixdown ready for mastering. If you want a limited loud mix for direct SoundCloud posting, let me know and I will provide that alongside the unmastered mix.

How should I organize my vocal tracks?+

Label your tracks clearly before exporting: Main Vox, Main Double, Adlibs, Harmonies, Backing. Put them all in a folder named with your artist name and track title, zip the folder, and upload it.

How do I send you the files?+

Upload your zipped folder to Google Drive, Dropbox, or WeTransfer (ensure link sharing is set to "Anyone with the link can view/download"). Then DM me the link on Instagram or SoundCloud along with your reference track and creative vision.

Who owns the rights and royalties to the music?+

You own your music 100%. Saint Gordon is about building skills, discovering new voices, and making genuine underground art—not exploiting royalties. You decide how, when, and where your music is published.

Send me what you’re working on.

Drop me a message with your demo or stem link, whether you need a vocal mix or a feature, your reference track, and any specific ideas you have in mind.
